speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury involving a jersey pull is very suggestive of a specific ligament injury. Was your finger displaced to the side during this event, and do you feel instability or clicking when you try to move it?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray (Right hand AP and Lateral) to rule out fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling is noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion fracture of the extensor hood at the DIP joint).

The history of a direct blow causing the finger to extend while you tried to make a fist, combined with your inability to actively flex the distal joint and the resting extension, confirms this injury. I am disregarding the previous mention of "Pyelonephritis" as it is clinically inconsistent with localized finger trauma.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
